run_findings.generic_checks_readback_revision: No dedicated general Checks action was discovered, but generic read-only GitHub.fetch accepts public REST check-runs and check-suites endpoints. On public github/docs exact main SHA 1beae09958f6eac6a4d82e5ee902d67f28dddda6, check-runs returned 42 entries and a filtered archives/app_id=15368 query returned completed/success on the exact SHA. Dedicated get_commit_combined_status returned only classic statuses and is not a Checks substitute. Private-repository Checks permission/exposure remains unverified.
run_findings.effective_policy_boundary: Generic fetch can read public ruleset list/detail and exposed github/docs ruleset 19633356 applying to refs/heads/main with required reviews, non-fast-forward, merge_queue, and app-bound required status checks. GitHub's ideal REST effective-rules endpoint /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch} is documented but rejected by the current connector allowlist. Legacy branch-protection GET is connector-routable but requires Administration(read); the public github/docs probe returned 403. Therefore general full-policy inventory remains conditional and missing policy must be UNKNOWN.
run_findings.required_check_verifier: When policy inventory and required commit SHA are complete, verify both Check runs and commit statuses on the exact SHA. Required checks may be success/skipped/neutral; if a Check and status share a required name both must pass; app-bound rules require matching integration identity. For >1000 suites use suite-by-suite enumeration. Any permission/pagination/provenance gap is UNKNOWN.
run_findings.merge_queue_boundary: A required merge_queue changes the decisive evidence target from PR head to a queue-generated merge-group SHA. Current connector exposes no queue enqueue/async merge mutation. Public GitHub GraphQL enqueuePullRequest(expectedHeadOid) and current REST merge-async(sha, merge_action=merge_queue/default) provide exact-head queue-aware handoff benchmarks, but are not direct connected mutations here.
run_findings.composite_branch_cas_counterexample: The REST composite read H0 -> create C(parent=H0) -> non-force update_ref(C) is not strict CAS under force rewind. If a competitor rewinds head from H0 to ancestor A, C remains a descendant of A so A->C is a valid fast-forward and the update can succeed despite head != H0. GraphQL createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=H0) directly checks head equality and is stronger.
run_findings.atomic_multi_ref_benchmark: GitHub GraphQL updateRefs performs multiple ref creates/updates/deletes atomically and supports per-ref beforeOid preconditions, all-zero nonexistence assertions and deletion. Current connector exposes no generic GraphQL mutation; connected file/ref operations remain per-object/staged rather than equivalent multi-object atomic CAS.
run_findings.final_gate_verdict: Use PROVED_READY only with complete applicable policy inventory, exact required evidence identities, all evidence families passing, and no unresolved bypass ambiguity. Use PROVED_BLOCKED when a known requirement fails. Any unseen policy family, permission/pagination gap, unknown required SHA, queue-stage evidence gap, or bypass uncertainty forces UNKNOWN/fail-closed.
